AcmeConfig.description: Automatic certificates over ACME (Let's Encrypt and compatible servers).

ca_root_path.description:
PEM file with the CA that signs the ACME server's own TLS certificate.
Needed for a private ACME server (step-ca, Pebble); public providers
are trusted through the system roots.

domains.description: Domains to request a certificate for.

email.description: Contact addresses registered with the ACME account.

renew_before_days.description: Renew this many days before expiry.

storage_dir.description: Where the account key and issued certificate are kept.

AcmeStatus.description: What the admin API reports about certificate automation.

last_attempt_epoch_s.description: Epoch seconds of the last attempt, successful or not.

last_error.description: Why the last attempt failed, when it did.

AdminAuth.description:
How the admin API checks a caller.

`none` is only legal on a loopback listener: a control plane that can
rewrite the proxy's config must not be reachable without a credential.

AdminConfig.description:
The `[admin]` block.

The credential itself never lives here. `token_file` and `basic_file`
point at a file (or, when unset, the `PRX_ADMIN_TOKEN` / `PRX_ADMIN_BASIC`
environment variables), so a config that is shown, diffed or committed
cannot carry the secret.

allow_origins.description:
Origins allowed to call the API from another site. Empty means
same-origin only; `*` is never valid.

basic_file.description:
Path to a file holding `user:password`, one line. Ignored unless
`auth` is `basic`.

read_only.description: Serve the API for reading and refuse every change.

token_file.description:
Path to a file holding the bearer token, one line. Ignored unless
`auth` is `token`.

plugins.description:
The [[plugin]] blocks as declared, so the UI can list what a route may
refer to (T501).

config.description:
The plugin's own settings, whose shape depends on `kind`. Passed
through as JSON rather than typed here, for the same reason the config
keeps it as a raw TOML value.

AdminRoutePayload.description:
A route exactly as the config holds it.

The advanced blocks travel with it because the UI is the only editor most
people will use: a payload that leaves out header rules, limits or cache
settings turns "edit this route" into "lose whatever the file said about
them".

plugins.description: Names of the [[plugin]] blocks this route runs, in order (T501).

h2c.description: Accept HTTP/2 over cleartext on the plain listeners.

AdminServicePayload.description:
A service exactly as the config holds it.

Same reasoning as `AdminRoutePayload`: the UI is the only editor most people
will use, so a payload that leaves out health checks, session affinity or
retry budgets turns "edit this service" into "lose them".

acme.description:
Automatic certificates, so the Settings page can show and edit them
without a second request (T308).

cert_path.description: Present only for the single-certificate form.

certs.description: The `[[server.tls.cert]]` blocks, as the file has them.

CacheConfig.description:
Short-lived response cache for a route.

Even a one-second TTL turns a burst of identical requests into a single
upstream fetch, which is where most of the benefit comes from.

add_status_header.description: Add an `X-Cache: HIT|MISS` header to responses.

coalesce_wait_ms.description:
How long a coalesced request waits for the in-flight fetch before going
upstream itself.

key_query.description: Include the query string in the cache key.

max_body_bytes.description: Responses larger than this are streamed through without being stored.

vary_headers.description:
Request headers whose values take part in the cache key, so responses
that differ by them are not mixed up.

CompressionConfig.description:
Response compression.

prx uses pingora's streaming compressor, so a large response is compressed
as it flows through rather than being buffered first.

decompress_upstream.description:
Decompress an already-compressed upstream response when the client
cannot accept that encoding. Off by default: it is expensive and rarely
what an operator wants.

level.description:
Compression level. Higher costs CPU for a smaller body; 3-6 is the
usual range for a proxy that compresses on the fly.

ConcurrencyLimitConfig.description: Caps how many requests a route may have in flight at once.

ConfigConflict.description:
What a client gets back when its `If-Match` no longer matches the file:
enough to show the three sides without a second request.

expected_etag.description: What the client believed it was editing.

Diagnostic.description:
One problem, addressed both by field path and by file position.

Positions are 1-based, and columns count characters rather than bytes so a
file with Thai comments in it still marks the right column.

EditAction.description: What to do to one key.

oneOf.description: Write `value` at `path`, creating the tables it needs.
Delete the key, or the array-of-tables element, at `path`.
Push a new `[[path]]` element built from `value`.

path.description:
Dotted path, with `[i]` for an array-of-tables element:
`server.tls.acme.domains`, `service[0].upstream[1].weight`.

value.description: The new value, as JSON. Ignored by `remove`.

EditRequest.description:
`POST /web/config/edit` (T308): the Settings forms change one field at a
time, and the answer is the same file with that field changed.

toml.description:
The draft to edit — normally what the editor is showing, not the file on
disk, so form edits and hand edits pile up in the same draft.

valid.description:
True when nothing would stop this config from being applied. Warnings
do not make it false.

HeaderRules.description:
Header rules applied to a request or a response.

`set` replaces any existing value, `add` appends another value, and
`remove` drops the header. They are applied in that order, so a rule set
can normalize a header and then append to it.

HeadersConfig.description: Header rules that apply to every route, applied before the route's own.

HealthCheckConfig.description:
Background probing of a service's upstreams.

Passive detection (the circuit breaker) only removes an upstream after real
requests have already failed, so users see the errors. An active probe finds
the same failure before a request does, and proves an upstream is healthy
again before sending traffic back to it.

expected_status.description: Response codes that count as healthy for `kind = "http"`.

healthy_threshold.description: Consecutive successes before a down upstream is used again.

unhealthy_threshold.description: Consecutive failures before an upstream is taken out.

oneOf.description: Open a TCP connection and close it again.
Send a GET and check the status code.

IssueSeverity.description:
How much a [`ConfigIssue`] matters: an error blocks the apply, a warning
does not.

oneOf.description:
Send the request to whichever of two random upstreams has fewer
requests in flight. Power of two choices avoids scanning every
upstream while getting most of the benefit of true least-connections.

Like `least_conn`, but weighted by a moving average of each upstream's
latency, so a slow-but-accepting upstream is avoided too.

PluginConfig.description:
One `[[plugin]]` block.

`config` is left as a raw TOML value because what belongs in it is decided
by `kind`: the registry checks it, not this struct. Keeping it opaque here
is what stops every new plugin from having to add a field to the core
config type.

admin.description: The control plane: where the admin API listens and how it is guarded.

plugin.description:
Plugins are declared once here and referenced by name from the routes
that want them, the same way a route references a service (T501).

waf.description: SecLang rules for the WAF. Empty unless `[waf] rules_file` is set.

RateLimitConfig.description:
Per-route rate limiting.

Cheap enough to leave on: one hash and a short lock on a sharded bucket per
request, with a hard cap on how many keys are tracked so a flood of unique
keys cannot grow memory without bound.

burst.description: How many requests may arrive at once before the sustained rate applies.

entry_ttl_ms.description: Keys idle for this long may be forgotten.

retry_after.description: Send a `Retry-After` header with the rejection.

enabled.description:
A disabled route stays in the file but is left out of the route index,
so it never matches — the way to park a route without losing how it was
configured.

plugins.description:
Plugins to run for this route, in this order (T501). Names refer to
`[[plugin]]` blocks.

last_probe_ms_ago.description: How long ago the prober last checked, when the verdict came from it.

source.description:
Where this verdict came from: the background prober, or a TCP connect
opened just to answer this request.

RouteStats.description: A route's share of the last minute.

RouteTestRequest.description: "If a request like this arrived, where would it go?"

request.description: The request as the matcher saw it, after host normalization.

matched_by.description:
Which tier of the matching rules this route won on: `exact_host`,
`wildcard_host`, `any_host`, or `default_route` when it only caught the
request as the fallback.

deterministic.description:
False for the strategies that draw at random: there is no single
upstream to name, and pretending otherwise would be a guess.

available.description: Whether this upstream is in the running for the next request.

Sample.description: One second of traffic, as rates rather than counters.

cache_hit_ratio.description: `None` when no route has caching turned on.

error_ratio_4xx.description: Share of requests in this second that answered 4xx / 5xx, in 0..1.

p50_ms.description:
`None` while no request finished in the window: a percentile over zero
requests is not zero milliseconds.

window_seconds.description: Seconds this sample covers; a late tick widens it rather than lying.

h2c.description:
Accept HTTP/2 over cleartext on the plain listeners. prx peeks for the
h2 preface and falls back to HTTP/1.1, so leaving this on is safe and
is what gRPC clients that do not use TLS need.

health_check.description:
Probe upstreams in the background instead of waiting for a real request
to discover that one is down.

request_timeout_ms.description: Total time budget for a request including every retry. `0` disables it.

retry_budget_min_per_window.description:
Requests below this count per window may always retry, so a service
that is idle or just started is not locked out by its own budget.

retry_budget_ratio.description:
Fraction of recent successful requests that may be spent on retries.
`0.0` disables the budget (retries are then limited only by
`max_retries`). Keeps a failing upstream from being hammered by the
retries of every in-flight request at once.

retry_budget_window_ms.description: Window the retry budget is measured over.

retry_idempotent_only.description:
Only retry requests whose method is idempotent once the request may
already have reached the upstream. Connect failures are always
retriable: nothing was sent yet.

sticky.description: Keep a client on the same upstream across requests.

upstream_h2.description: Which HTTP version to speak to the upstreams of this service.

health_check_enabled.description: Whether the background prober is running for this service at all.

ServiceStatusPayload.description:
Live state of every service, as the running proxy sees it right now.

The config says what was asked for; this says what is happening. The page
that shows circuit breakers and probe verdicts needs the second one, and it
has to come from the same snapshot traffic is being routed on.

StatsEvent.description: Something worth a line in the dashboard's event strip.

id.description: Monotonic, so a reconnecting client can tell what it already has.

target.description: The route, service or domain the event is about, when there is one.

StatsSnapshot.description:
The first payload a dashboard reads, so the page has a chart before the
stream has said anything.

StickyConfig.description:
Session affinity: keep a client on the upstream it used last.

`cookie` is the only mode that survives a client changing IP, and it is the
only one that pins exactly; `client_ip` and `header` hash the key onto the
upstream ring, so adding or removing an upstream reshuffles some clients.
Every mode falls back to normal load balancing when the chosen upstream is
unavailable, so affinity never costs availability.

name.description: Cookie or header name, depending on the mode.

ttl_s.description: Lifetime of the cookie in `cookie` mode.

oneOf.description: prx sets a cookie naming the upstream and honors it on later requests.
Hash the value of a request header.

TlsCertConfig.description: One certificate and the domains it answers for.

domains.description:
Domains this certificate serves. `*.example.com` also covers
`example.com`. Left empty, the names are read from the certificate
itself.

is_default.description: Used for clients that send no SNI, or a name no certificate covers.

cert.description: Certificates to choose from by SNI.

cert_path.description:
Single-certificate form, kept so existing configs keep working. Prefer
`[[server.tls.cert]]`, which supports more than one domain.

certificates.description: Certificates the running listener would serve right now.

enabled.description:
`false` drains the upstream: it stays in the config, keeps being probed,
and is left out of the selection ring so it takes no traffic.

This cannot be expressed as `weight = 0` — the balancer clamps weights to
at least 1, so a zero-weight upstream would quietly keep serving.

UpstreamH2.description:
How prx talks to a service's upstreams.

gRPC needs `always`: it requires end-to-end HTTP/2 because it carries its
status in trailers, which HTTP/1.1 cannot express.

oneOf.description:
HTTP/2 only. Over TLS this is negotiated with ALPN; over cleartext prx
trusts that the upstream speaks h2c.

Prefer HTTP/2, fall back to HTTP/1.1. Over cleartext there is no ALPN to
negotiate with, so this behaves like `never`.
Turned off in the config — not a failure, and not counted as one.

circuit_reopens_in_ms.description: Milliseconds until the breaker closes again, when it is open.

enabled.description: False when the upstream is drained: still configured, taking no traffic.

share.description: Share of the selection ring, read from the ring itself.

ValidateResponse.description:
`POST /web/config/validate` (T203): every problem in one pass, each with the
line it is on, and nothing written.

config.description:
The config as the API would report it, when it is valid — so the editor
can say what changed without parsing TOML in the browser.

current_etag.description:
The ETag of the file on disk at the moment of validation. A draft whose
base no longer matches this was overtaken by someone else.

valid.description:
True when nothing would stop this config from being applied. Warnings
do not make it false.

True when nothing would stop this config from being applied. Warnings
do not make it false.

id.description: `<unix ms>-<fingerprint>`; what rollback is asked for.

WafConfig.description: The `[waf]` block. Absent means no rules, so the WAF does nothing.

inbound_anomaly_threshold.description:
Summed anomaly score at which a request is blocked. Must be positive.
Unset means 5.

paranoia_level.description:
CRS paranoia level, 1 to 4. Only rules at or below this level count
toward blocking. Unset means 1. Kept as `i64` so that out-of-range
values reach `check` as a `ConfigIssue` instead of a parse error.

rules_file.description:
A SecLang rules file. A relative path resolves against the directory
of the config file.
